method: Every source frame decoded to deterministic change features; all 215 representative frames on 18 sheets visually inspected. No direct audio listening; not every frame visually examined. Grouped notes do not replace per-state annotations.

notes.observation: Photographic modern skyline/highway backgrounds carry a pink-robed cartoon presenter, coin growth graphic and red X. Two cartoon car owners exchange on-screen dialogue. Large desert title THE RISE OF DUBAI and 120 YEARS AGO establish chronological framing.

Simple boat and diver illustration, photographic pearls and pearl-ring radial backdrop precede a Dubai map character with pearl sacks. Dialogue celebrates a future that the 1929 date immediately reverses. This is illustrative dialogue, not historical testimony.

Japan map and cartoon laboratory with CULTURED PEARLS text lead to world-map pearl/currency markers. Dubai character calls pearls worthless and rejects them on black background. Date/causality claims remain unverified.

EARLY 1900s date, regional maps, archival-looking footage and forbidden laptop/book icons accompany the presenter. Archive identity and geographic accuracy are not verified; icons are narrative simplifications.

US flag-map character introduces oil demand. Desert oil rigs, repeated dialogue and trucks dramatize exploration. Screen labels distinguish 1958 Abu Dhabi and 1966 Dubai; the caption narrative dates a British departure earlier. Sheikh Rashid portrait is explicitly labeled.

Oil-rig dialogue, 1966 date, offshore platform drawing, pipe illustration, oil trucks and an archival-looking group photo carry ENTER THE MODERN AGE. Extraction/source and licensing of archival assets are unknown.

Regional historical map precedes an incremental emirate map label build and UAE flag. Anthropomorphic Bahrain/Qatar maps decline joining; Abu Dhabi versus Dubai matchup graphic introduces disagreement. No archival basis is implied for dramatized dialogue.

1960/1980 pictures show a 276,000 population label. Bar graphic TOTAL OIL BARRELS MADE labels Abu Dhabi 92 billion, Dubai 4 billion, Sharjah 1.5 billion. Caption describes reserves; production-versus-reserves wording needs review. Separate scene shows 57% GDP. These source graphics are not independently verified economic data.

Leader cartoon with shrinking-oil thought bubble introduces an attributed camel/vehicle quotation built line by line, then paired pearl/oil assets and archival-looking drilling footage. Quote attribution and wording require a primary source.

1979 date, money collage, isolated World Trade Center photos, industrial footage, port photography, animated container vessel and labeled Dubai Aluminum Smelter build an infrastructure sequence. Leader and skyline collages contrast with other map characters. Photo dates not certified.

Solar/industrial building, container ship and Emirates aircraft cutouts precede FREE TRADE / INFRASTRUCTURE / TOURISM. Palm Jumeirah 2001, Burj Khalifa 2004 and Dubai Mall 2008 appear as source labels; later views emphasize 88% Foreigners. Photographs may illustrate project-start dates rather than have those capture dates.

Travel world map with curved routes precedes a satellite view labeled Dubai, UAE 2000. A cartoon camel/worker and illustrated newspaper SLAVERY ENDS! display 1963. This drawn newspaper is not documentary proof.

Construction-site background and helmeted worker/boss characters dramatize denied time off. Worker group shrinks to one and illness dialogue appears. These are visual storytelling observations; mortality/abuse statistics need independent evidence.

Dubai map, a timeline with 1967 oil and 1985 Emirates, then GDP charts and palm-island aerial view form the conclusion. A historical oil-share graph begins around 80% in 1950 despite earlier discovery narrative in 1966; series/methodology absent. Trading-port status index is similarly undefined.

TIME text hands off to a Swiss map, warfare art, historical Swiss maps, law/governance cartoon and closing presenter. This is a cross-video Switzerland recommendation; footage reuse is visible within the recommendation, not independent Swiss analysis.
